figures.finding: Namibia's national fund is the Namibia Film Commission's Film and Video Fund, for Namibian producers developing, producing and distributing film, video and TV projects of Namibian origin; it prioritises features, drama, documentary and animation for cinema, TV or streaming, prefers Namibian writers, directors and producers, requires the work to take place in Namibia, counts two screen credits as 'experienced', and runs one call a year (the 2026 call closed on 10 August 2026). No share, cap or selection rate is published.

value.name: Film and Video Fund (Namibia Film Commission)
value.for: Namibian producers, projects of Namibian origin

sources.said: The Film and Video Fund, initiated by the Namibia Film Commission (NFC), plays a crucial role in the establishment and growth of the film industry in Namibia. The fund is designed to provide financial assistance to Namibian film producers, enabling them to develop, produce, and distribute captivating film, video, and television projects of Namibian origin.

The NFC gives priority to project funding in the areas of feature films, drama, documentary, and animation. … Preference will be given to projects that involve Namibian writers, directors, and/or producers. … All funded activities, including industry and audience development activities, must take place within Namibia … with a minimum requirement of two screen credits to qualify as an experienced filmmaker.
Applications for this year closed on 10 August 2026 .

figures.finding: Namibia publishes no production rebate; a foreign production needs a film permit from the Namibia Film Commission (script, synopsis, schedule and budget), must work with a local production company, must use Namibian crew unless skills are lacking, and its non-Namibian crew, SADC included, need work visas even for one day.

value.workVisas: all non-Namibian crew, incl. SADC, even 1 day

sources.said: Filmmakers are generally required to obtain a film permit from the Namibian Film Commission (NFC) before commencing any filming activities in Namibia. … Working with a local production company is a requirement when obtaining a film permit.
the use of Namibian crew is a requirement unless there is skills deficit.
All non-Namibian crew, even crew from SADC countries, require work visas to film in Namibia, even if it is only for a 1-day shoot.
